info.title: Skysay API
info.description: Agent-native telephony API for customer onboarding, credits, numbers, webhooks, gateways, and policy-gated calls. Request bodies are UTF-8. Send JSON: a body that is absent or whitespace-only reads as an empty object, and a JSON body that is not valid JSON, is not a JSON object, or is not UTF-8 returns 400. (The provider-callback routes that have always accepted application/x-www-form-urlencoded or text/plain still do.) A request carrying any Content-Encoding other than identity returns 415 — this API does not accept compressed request bodies. A required field that is missing, null or blank returns 400 naming the field.

get.description: Returns the read-only data needed by the Numbers dashboard, including workspace-wide number_allowance (used, limit, remaining, can_add; null limit means no billed-number cap). Each number includes calling_readiness: bounded inbound routing/pricing blockers and destination-dependent outbound configuration. Outbound registration_status distinguishes pending, failed, registered, not_required and legacy; pending or failed caller-ID registration blocks outbound only and is retried independently of carrier-ready inbound activation. DIDWW capacity pricing can report capacity_hybrid_unsupported, capacity_separate_metering_unsupported, or capacity_plan_unavailable; these refuse only the affected number. Inbound readiness remains indeterminate when mandatory call-time admission checks were not evaluated; a purchased number is not proof that calls can connect. The aggregate is tenant-bound to the bearer session, makes no provider calls or writes, and excludes provider internals, secrets, unrelated billing history, calls, SMS, and verification documents. An exact request return may include the most recent confirmed positive Stripe top-up summary for conversion capture. Pass project_id for an explicit project; when omitted, the response returns its selected default project. Bounded collections expose truncation flags rather than silently implying a complete export.

parameters.name: number_request_id
parameters.description: Optional exact request in the authenticated workspace project. An unavailable selection returns no selected request so the bounded Numbers list remains usable; never selects another request.

get.summary: Read the bounded, customer-scoped Calls aggregate
get.description: Public customer API for the Calls workspace view: the newest page of call history with its real total, the selected call's observability detail, the workspace agents, the latest trial, and the compact wallet snapshot the shared workspace header uses. It also reports, per call, which workflow version ran and a compact path through it -- step ids, chosen routes, tool statuses and sanitized policy reasons -- plus the full turn-grouped trace for the selected call. A selected transcript turn's has_audio flag is true only while an active recording and its linked turn clip are available; clients use the authenticated recording relay rather than a storage or artifact identifier. A call that ran no workflow is ABSENT from workflow_evidence rather than present and empty. The selected call's transcript also carries one server-ordered timeline interleaving its turns with the typed tool calls the agent finished and the language switches it made, ordered on the recording clock with a single truncation flag for both sources; turn entries reference the turns returned beside them rather than repeating their text. The selected call's waveform carries at most 256 peaks (a longer stored series is max-pooled, never cut) and speaker_segments: who spoke when on the recording's own clock, each with turn_id, speaker (agent or caller), start_ms and end_ms, projected only from turns whose boundary was measured on that recording, bounded by the same turn slice and reported with speaker_segments_truncated; a moment no segment covers is unattributed, not silent. The selected call's counterparty carries the other person's phone_e164 (the number called, or the caller's number on an inbound call; empty for a browser test) and contact_name, the name that number is saved under in this organization's contacts (the newest when several lists hold it; empty when none). Those rows are typed only: a tool entry carries its closed kind, an opaque reference, ok, a closed error class and a duration, and the configured tool name is resolved for display from the call's own agent configuration rather than stored - tool arguments, results, URLs, response bodies and error messages are never recorded. Each capability reports its own status and a closed reason, so a call handled before this existed, a gateway-imported call, a workflow call or an engine that does not record language switches is explicit about it and never reads as a call that made no tool calls. Bound to the bearer session organization; it never accepts an arbitrary organization, calls a provider, reconciles state, or writes data. The call's internal runtime configuration is never returned, and neither is a run's pinned contract. Both the path per row and the trace are bounded and report truncation; detail=0 omits the selected call's observability and its trace for routine freshness polls. Every response echoes calls_source_kind, the provenance it actually answered for, and calls_has_more, which says whether an older page exists -- observed by reading one row past the limit, never inferred from a page that happens to be full. Each call row carries source_kind, from the same closed set as the query parameter. The selected call's observability carries call_variables and its trace carries variables_evidence; call_variables lists what admission froze for the call -- each declared variable and built-in with its name, type, source (builtin, or the call's source: api, campaign, inbound_lookup, browser_test, simulation, trial), protected, requires and state -- plus the committed confirmation record (method, match_kind, step_id, step_name, turn_index, committed_at), bounded with limit, returned and has_more; state is ready, not_admitted (no snapshot) or unreadable. A value is returned only for an ordinary variable in state shown; a protected variable never carries a value, before or after confirmation, only its state: held (until a confirmation releases it) or released with released_at_turn. variables_evidence lists the run's knowledge_match outcomes (match, mismatch, abstain) and workflow SMS-step statuses (pending, sending, sent, failed, uncertain, recorded) in run order from one bounded read, with limit, returned and has_more; never an answer, a compared value, an SMS body, a recipient or a failure text.

parameters.name: project_id
parameters.description: Optional project in the authenticated organization.

parameters.name: call_id
parameters.description: Optional canonical call ID in the selected project; it is resolved and pinned even when older than the newest page. A call_id that is not in the authenticated organization, the selected project and the requested source_kind is answered with selected_call_not_found=true, an empty selected_call_id and no selected call or detail -- never with a different call in its place; the page of calls is returned as usual. Without call_id the newest call is selected.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Maximum calls in the returned page.

parameters.name: detail
parameters.description: Set to 0 for a freshness poll: the selected call's observability and full workflow trace are omitted, the per-row workflow evidence is not.

parameters.name: source_kind
parameters.description: Which calls the page is about. `live` -- the default, and what this route has always returned -- is a call a customer or a caller actually made. `simulation_suite` is a Simulations Lab call: a real call row with the customer's own agent in it and a synthetic caller on the other end, created by the lab to run a scenario. The two are separate views of the same page, never mixed: one request answers for one provenance, and every figure in the response -- the page, calls_total, the selected call and the workflow evidence -- is about that provenance alone. A value outside this set is a 400 rather than a silent fall back to `live`.

parameters.name: before
parameters.description: A `page_cursor` from a row of a previous page. The response continues strictly older than that ROW, so calls created since do not shift the page under you the way an offset would. Opaque: its encoding is not part of this contract.

get.summary: Read the bounded, customer-scoped Agents aggregate
get.description: Returns one tenant-bound Agents DTO for SSR. It includes resolved static voice-stack display data, which components the customer actually configured (as opposed to the catalog defaults the resolved stack fills in), every language each agent answers in (`selected_languages`, which is the agent's own `language` alone for an agent whose owner never chose a language set -- `language` remains the one that OPENS the call), an inbound-admission verdict per agent, attached number routing, exact UTC-day activity, each agent's measured reply time (the median of its recorded worker-side reply turns, or an explicit unavailable when nothing was measured -- never a component-constant estimate presented as an observation), and wallet currency without provider or catalog API calls, verification, invoice, SMS, or webhook service reads. The admission verdict is a pure read of workspace state: `admits`/`readiness` reflect only conditions the inbound call path itself would refuse over; `blockers` is not a strict subset of those -- a small, explicitly declared set of codes (currently a misconfigured transfer_to_human destination) is real and actionable but does not affect `admits`/`readiness`, because invoking that tool mid-call fails gracefully rather than refusing the call. `unevaluated` lists the conditions the read could not evaluate before a call exists, and `readiness` is blocked or indeterminate — never ready, because the gates that need the agent's number are not run here. A line-scoped readiness is reported by the Overview aggregate's primary_line. An agent answered by the customer's own service is judged on the endpoints it needs rather than on the managed stack it does not use. Soft-deleted agents are not part of the workspace: they are excluded from `agents` and from `total_agents`.

get.summary: Read the bounded, customer-scoped hosted-agent editor aggregate
get.description: Returns one selected agent, its resolved stack including saved turn_taking, voice_polish, answer_detection and audio_environment settings, which components were actually configured (for a voice the agent never stored, voice_stack.language_profiles.default_voices names the default voice model of each supported language the shown voice cannot run, so a language added in the editor gets one too), the same inbound-admission verdict the Agents list carries, the runnable-adapter catalog (each entry carrying component_metered, so the launch-supported view is one filter over it rather than a second copy), a wallet projection, a bounded metadata-only BYOK credential list, and the agent's measured reply time: the median of a bounded sample of its recorded worker-side reply turns, reported as unavailable rather than zero until real calls exist. That figure ends when the first audio frame leaves the worker, so carrier transit and remote playout are not in it. It is bound to the dashboard session organization and selected project; it never decrypts credentials, calls a provider, validates a key, or writes state. It also carries `call_variables`: the AI agent's normalized call-variables config (declared fields, SMS templates, SMS mode, caller lookup), the `revision` a write names as `base_revision`, the `schema` its calls are admitted with (a published workflow's variables when one is active, with `workflow_version` and the agent's own earlier fields as `superseded_fields`), whether its voice engine is live, its languages, and at most 50 of the project's contact lists for caller lookup, newest first, with `lookup_lists_has_more`. It is written only through `PUT /v1/agents/{agent_id}/variables`.

get.summary: Read the Billing history aggregate: usage by day or month and one page of the wallet ledger
get.description: Returns one read-only page DTO. `history` is wallet spend per UTC period (granularity `day` with periods up to 90, default 30; or `month` with periods up to 24, default 12; `end` optionally names the last day YYYY-MM-DD or month YYYY-MM), per category (`calls`, `sms`, `numbers`, `recordings`, `translations`, `other`), in the wallet's currency as integer minor units, with every period present. Spend is money the ledger recorded as spent; top-ups, refunds and call holds/releases are not spend. `ledger` is one page of wallet entries, newest first by (created_at, id), filtered by `type` (`all`, `topup`, `call`, `sms`, `number`, `recording`, `translation`, `refund`, `hold`, `other`) and an inclusive UTC date range `from`/`to` (YYYY-MM-DD, default the history window); pass `next_cursor` back as `cursor` while `has_more` is true. `matching_count` counts the filtered entries up to `export_row_cap`, and `matching_count_exceeds_export_cap` says the CSV export would be refused. `calls_split` divides the range's call spend into `phone_line_minor` (the carrier component's share of each hosted AI call, rounded down, or the whole of a call billed without hosted AI components) and `ai_agent_minor` (the rest); the two always add up to `calls_minor`. Each entry's `amount_minor` is how the entry reads to a customer: the amount spent, negative, for a charge (which is taken from an earlier hold), otherwise the change to available funds (a hold negative, its release positive, a credit positive); so amounts across a call's hold, charge and release do not sum to the balance change. `available_delta_minor` sums to the change in available funds and `spent_delta_minor` to spend. Entries carry only customer-safe fields: Stripe references in short form, a `call_id` only for a call in the same workspace, and an `sms_conversation_id` for an SMS charge. The ledger lists the whole organization's wallet, every project's entries alike, whatever `project_id` is passed (a `project_id` must belong to the session's organization, else 404). Each entry's `project_id` is the project of its call or SMS conversation (null when it has neither, or the conversation belongs to no project). The dashboard Calls and SMS pages read only the session's project, so the workspace links an entry's call or conversation only when the entry's `project_id` is that project. Tenant-bound to the bearer session; no provider request and no write.

400.description: A range, filter or cursor is out of bounds or malformed

404.description: The named project is not in the session's organization

get.summary: Export the filtered wallet ledger as CSV
get.description: Returns exactly the entries the Billing history ledger pages through for the same `type`, `from` and `to` (both required, YYYY-MM-DD, UTC, inclusive), in the same order, as `text/csv`. Columns: created_at, id, type, category, currency, amount (decimal), amount_minor, available_delta_minor, reserved_delta_minor, spent_delta_minor, promotional_spent_delta_minor, reference, call_id, sms_conversation_id, note. Integer minor-unit columns are the exact figures; amount_minor has the aggregate's meaning, available_delta_minor sums to the change in available funds and spent_delta_minor to spend. A file carries at most 10,000 entries: a larger selection is refused with 400 and a message asking for a shorter range, never truncated.

get.summary: Read the workspace's capabilities record, the selectable use-case profiles, and live usage against its caps
get.description: Pure read. Every workspace has exactly one record from creation on: `capabilities.status` is `not_activated` until the workspace clears verification (an operator's business review, or its first registration-free number), when it becomes `active` on the default profile, the channels the workspace holds and every destination except the sanctioned set (`all_countries: true`). `pending_review` means a request is with an Skysay operator and nothing new is authorized yet; `suspended` means an operator paused outbound. When `all_countries` is false, `countries` is the explicit allowlist (ISO 3166-1 alpha-2). `calling_rules` is the application cadence contract an operator recorded on approval, or null, and `calling_rules_active` says whether it is enforced right now. Every outbound call and SMS is authorized against this record (see POST /v1/policies/authorize-outbound).

200.description: Capabilities record, calling rules, available profiles and usage

403.description: The credential does not belong to this organization

post.summary: Request or change the workspace's capabilities
post.description: Select the use-case profiles, channels and destinations outbound should be authorized for, and accept the outbound policy by sending `policy_version`. The destination choice is explicit: `all_countries: true` (every destination except the sanctioned set) or `countries` naming at least one well-formed ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code. A request with neither, with an empty list, or with an entry that is not a two-letter code is refused with 400 and nothing is written, so an active allowlist is never widened or emptied by a request that was refused. A verified workspace that accepts the policy and selects no custom profile is activated immediately within the profiles' default caps; anything else opens an Skysay review, and what is already active stays active until the review resolves. `calling_rules` cannot be set here; an operator records them on approval.

get.description: Pass metered_only=true to receive only the launch-supported hosted components with a runtime adapter, native meter, pinned retail rate, and safe credential contract (validated BYOK where supported or an explicit platform-managed provider contract). The payload also includes conversation_engines: cascade (default STT/LLM/TTS) and gpt_live (GPT-Live-1 voices and Responses backends). Every engine row carries has_language_axis: true for cascade, false for a voice-to-voice engine that has no separate transcriber, LLM or TTS and therefore no language set, no per-language profile overrides and no Follow the caller. Read that flag rather than matching on the engine id: agent create and the voice-stack PATCH refuse languages / language_profiles / follow_caller for an engine whose row says false. A TTS row uses either immutable worker-approved voices or bounded provider-directory voices already ingested by Skysay; the catalog never fetches a provider during a read. Voice metadata and tags are provider-supplied and carry provenance; Skysay does not infer age, accent, or personality. When a provider supplies no per-voice language list, the row inherits only its qualified TTS model languages. voice_count and voices_truncated say when a provider inventory is partial. A resolved agent preserves its exact selected voice in its voice-stack response even outside a bounded catalog slice. Every TTS row carries `delivery_control`: `voice_settings`, `instruction` or `speed` when a `voice_polish.delivery` profile changes that engine's audio, or `unsupported` when the engine accepts and stores a profile without changing its audio (Fish Audio and Azure neural voices today); and `delivery_profiles`, the exact value each of the four profiles resolves to on that engine (a settings object such as stability/similarity_boost/style/speed, a speaking rate, or an instruction sentence), empty for `unsupported`. Both are read from the same packaged delivery table the call runtime and the voice preview use, so a client can state what a profile changes for a voice without a provider list of its own. Each tts entry also lists default_languages: the languages in `languages` where the voice may be chosen WITHOUT the owner choosing it (for example as the pre-selected voice of a new agent). A voice can run a language without being its default -- ElevenLabs eleven_v3 runs English but lists only Estonian -- and a client that pre-selects voices should respect it. This catalog does not authorize a provider credential or disclose provider secrets.

It accepts a bounded caller sentence (defaulting to a short product sample only when no audio_environment is supplied), keeps no audio or telemetry, and returns a short in-memory WAV only. A selected outgoing audio_environment requires explicit non-blank text and makes a deterministic, headroom-safe local audition; it never substitutes the text, language, voice, or claims a receiver-side final mix. A small per-workspace fixed-window limit protects provider spend. Every language a provider advertises can be previewed. On a platform credential the voice must be one the workspace could browse and select, except an existing saved hosted agent may re-test its exact current platform-managed selection by supplying agent_id when it has disappeared from a listing; arbitrary typed IDs never create shared runtime evidence. With a selected BYOK credential the credential is validated at the provider and then used to render, so any voice id that provider accepts works, and a platform credential is never a fallback. A GPT-Live-1 voice (provider openai, model gpt-live-1) previews differently: it is a short real live session on the platform credential that speaks Skysay's own sample sentence for the requested language, rendered once per voice, language and sample and then served from a tenant-agnostic cache (the response carries text_source: platform_sample and cached). scenarios.description: Authored caller scenarios. At most 50 per suite. Each scenario's turns carry what the caller does and when: kind is speech, backchannel or silence; a silence turn carries silence_ms and no caller_input, because a silence is time rather than words; cue.after_agent_turn (1-based, and 0 meaning no cue at all: take the turn when the agent finishes) and cue.delay_ms record where inside an observed agent turn the caller speaks. Multiple cues anchored to the same turn share that observed origin, and an unobserved cue or incomplete schedule produces no scenario timing proof rather than an invented one. ground_truth_variants records alternative renderings of the same line -- a numeral written as digits or as words, say -- so a run's stored evidence carries what the caller was authored to say in every form that counts as correct. The platform's own offline recognition metric still scores against caller_input alone; the variants are carried for the readiness scorer that reads them. A silence turn needs the adaptive_voice runner and is refused with 422 silence_needs_a_room on any other, because only a room has time to spend. An adaptive_voice scenario may also carry caller_environment: a version-pinned synthetic caller MICROPHONE condition using noise_level (not the agent audio_environment volume). A scenario that supplies caller_environment must use adaptive_voice and also supply a non-blank language; it is never silently changed to English. Off/noise_level=0 is the quiet baseline; it never changes the agent's output ambience, TTS, or production STT configuration. A saved condition is authoring data, not proof that this deployment ran a realtime room.

post.summary: Ask a live call to hang up
post.description: Requests teardown of a call that is already live. This is also what the Hang up button on a live call in the workspace Calls page sends. Returns 202 with `hangup_requested_at`; it never reports the call as ended, because the media session is torn down by the worker holding it and the call reaches `call.ended` through the ordinary terminal path. The call then reports `ended_reason` `hangup_requested`, unless it had already started ending another way, in which case that ending's reason is reported. Repeating the request is idempotent and returns the original timestamp. Until a worker acknowledges, the request stays visible with `status` `pending`. If the worker reports that the teardown FAILED, the call is still up, so a further request re-arms it with a fresh timestamp and the previous failure's reason stays visible beside it; after three consecutive failed teardowns further requests are refused so the call is escalated rather than retried. A call still queued for origination is refused: cancel it with POST /v1/calls/{call_id}/cancel instead. For a workspace caller, a call in another workspace, or a Simulations Lab run, answers exactly as a call id that does not exist. The response carries `hangup_requested_at`, `status` (`pending` or `acknowledged`), `hangup_acknowledged_at`, `hangup_acknowledged_outcome`, `hangup_acknowledged_reason`, `hangup_failed_attempts`, `hangup_unacknowledged_seconds` (null once acknowledged), `hangup_attempt` (which attempt this is; a re-arm increments it) and `already_requested`, which is false for a first or re-armed request and true when an existing one was returned unchanged.

The switch is refused in either direction while calls are still in flight -- going local while outbound jobs are still queued would strand them, and going back to queue while the deployment is still dialing locally would abandon those calls. The separately operated platform_hosted mode is internal: it only authorizes an existing hosted call under its current worker lease, deriving tenant/configuration from that call, never creating a caller-selected tenant call. ApiKeyBearer.description: Scoped sky_ bearer keys are required by default for tenant/operator routes. Set SKYSAY_AUTH_MODE=development_open only for local demos.

currency.description: Must match wallet settlement currency when provided.

idempotency_key.description: Request-aware checkout uses the persisted claim even when a caller supplies a key.

number_request_id.description: Optional exact request context; never confirms, purchases or reserves a number.

Capabilities.description: The workspace's capabilities record: what it may do outbound. One per workspace, always. `active` authorizes outbound within the listed profiles, channels, destinations and limits; every other status authorizes nothing new.

destination_restrictions.description: Optional customer narrowing, intersected with current capabilities at admission. null means no additional customer restriction.

destination_revision.description: Revision required when saving optional destination restrictions.

all_countries.description: True: every destination except the sanctioned set is authorized and `countries` is empty. False: `countries` is the explicit allowlist. Activation through verification sets it true; a request chooses.

countries.description: The destination allowlist as ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 codes when `all_countries` is false. A call or text to any other country is held for review.

limits.description: The profile caps projected into the workspace's risk controls at its last activation or approval (per-day/per-minute call and SMS counts, unique destinations, daily voice and wallet spend in minor units). Empty when no profile caps were projected. The caps enforced right now are the workspace's risk controls, which an operator may have changed since; `/v1/dashboard/capabilities` reports those.

compliance_profile_id.description: The verified business profile the record was activated against; empty until verification clears.

customer_visible_message.description: Server-composed status sentence for the workspace; display as-is.

approved_by.description: `self_serve` for a request approved within the catalog, the operator who approved it, or the verification door that activated it.

calling_rules.description: The application calling rules an operator recorded on approval; `{}` when none apply.

CapabilitiesProfile.description: One selectable use-case profile and the caps it grants by default.

CapabilitiesUsage.description: Live usage for the same rolling windows the record's limits are expressed in.

CapabilitiesDetail.description: The record, its calling rules, the profiles the workspace may select from, and live usage against its caps.

calling_rules.description: The customer-visible projection of the application calling rules recorded during Skysay approval (effective period, time zone, calling windows, per-case cadence and attempt cap, escalation actions), or null when none apply. Configured by Skysay, never by this API.

calling_rules_active.description: True when calling rules are set and the record is active, i.e. they are enforced on every call right now.

profiles.description: At least one valid use-case profile. Unknown keys are dropped; a selection with none left is refused.

channels.description: Omitted or empty falls back to the selected profiles' own channels.

all_countries.description: True authorizes every destination except the sanctioned set and ignores `countries`. Exactly one of `all_countries: true` or a non-empty `countries` is required; a request with neither is refused with 400 and nothing is written.

countries.description: The destination allowlist as ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 codes, used when `all_countries` is not true. An empty list is refused, and so is any entry that is not a well-formed two-letter code once normalized (the refusal names it). A few aliases are normalized (UAE, USA, UK).

limits.description: Optional cap overrides; `live_call_concurrency` is always taken from the plan and never from this payload.

policy_version.description: Accepting the outbound policy here is what makes immediate activation possible for a verified workspace; without it the request goes to review.

metadata.description: Free-form notes merged into the record. `calling_rules` and the retired `metadata.operational_profile` key are refused here: calling rules are set during Skysay approval.

policy_version.description: Required unless the record already carries one.

events.description: Subscribed event types. Omitted or empty at creation defaults to call.created, call.answered, media.started, call.ended, call.completed, call.failed, call.canceled. Change it later with PATCH /v1/agent-endpoints/{agent_endpoint_id}. Subscribing to sms.received requires sms:read; call.extraction.ready requires recordings:read. Changing any endpoint destination requires both sms:read and recordings:read, including for queued deliveries and concurrent subscription changes.
The complete replacement subscription list; an empty array is rejected.

VoicePreviewRequest.description: One short synthesis of a bounded caller sentence for a selected TTS voice. Customer requests bind preview spend to the authenticated workspace; organization_id is an optional consistency hint and a foreign value is rejected.

organization_id.description: Optional consistency hint; if supplied, it must match the bearer workspace.

project_id.description: Must belong to the bearer workspace.

voice_id.description: Exact provider voice id. On a platform credential it must be present in the browsable voice inventory, except an existing saved hosted agent may explicitly re-test its exact current selection; with a BYOK credential any id the provider accepts is allowed, so cloned and private voices work.

language.description: Any language the selected provider advertises.

text.description: Optional sentence to speak. Omitted or blank falls back to a short product sample only when no audio_environment is supplied. With an audio_environment it is required and must be non-blank, so the requested text is never silently replaced. It is synthesized, never stored, and never echoed in the response.

audio_environment.description: Optional immutable ambience selection. When present, the preview WAV is a deterministic headroom-safe local audition only; this does not claim a receiver-side final mix. Provider voice and explicit language are unchanged.

delivery.description: Optional delivery profile, the same value an agent stores in `voice_polish.delivery`. The preview applies exactly the provider settings a call with that profile would use; for a provider/model without a truthful control (Fish Audio, Azure) the audio is unchanged and the response reports `delivery_applied: false`.

credential_id.description: Optional selected BYOK credential. It is validated at the provider and then used to render this preview; a platform credential is never a fallback.

agent_id.description: Optional saved hosted agent pin for a managed preview only. It must belong to the authenticated project and exactly match the requested platform-managed provider, model, voice id, and language. It permits re-testing a stored selection missing from the current provider listing; it does not authorize a new voice choice or any BYOK selection.

opening.description: Accepted at creation. Read and update the opening policy through the voice-stack route; the generic agent update route refuses this field.

oneOf.description: Exact selected TTS provider/model/voice inventory item.

voice_id.description: Provider inventory id, when the selected provider exposes voices.

languages.description: The languages this agent may answer in. An engine without a language axis (see voice_frontend and the agent-catalog conversation_engines block) REFUSES this field with 400 rather than accepting and dropping it.

language_profiles.description: When supplied this replaces the sparse override set; omit it to preserve overrides. Each item has locale and optional exact voice, transcriber, and greeting. Omitted values inherit the shared stack; an empty greeting removes its override.

follow_caller.description: Answer each caller in whichever selected language they speak. Accepted at creation so a multilingual agent can be created in one request; enabling it requires at least two languages and is refused with 400 otherwise. Creation stores the opt-in only -- the first PATCH /v1/agents/{agent_id}/voice-stack publication is what proves one shared transcriber can listen for the selected set, and refuses the publication when none can. Changing it afterwards is a voice-stack save, not an agent update. An engine without a language axis (see voice_frontend) REFUSES this field with 400 rather than accepting and dropping it.

AgentUpdate.description: Mutable agent configuration. The target agent, rather than organization_id or project_id in this body, defines the authenticated workspace boundary. Voice-stack settings are not part of this payload: opening, turn_taking, voice_polish, answer_detection, audio_environment, follow_caller, languages and language_profiles are saved by PATCH /v1/agents/{agent_id}/voice-stack, and sending one here is refused with 400 naming that route rather than accepted and dropped.

status.description: Whether this agent is offered to callers. `inactive` stops it being admitted on every call path -- inbound and outbound telephony, the browser test, and the public homepage demo -- while keeping the agent, its configuration and its number attachments intact; a call already in progress is not torn down. `active` removes that gate and nothing else: no configuration is snapshotted or restored, so the agent is then admitted on its CURRENT published configuration and readiness, which may have changed while it was inactive. Accepts these two values only; any other is refused with 400, as is any change to an agent whose stored status is not already one of them (an operator-suspended agent is reinstated by an operator only).

oneOf.description: Exact selected TTS provider/model/voice inventory item.

voice_id.description: Provider inventory id, when the selected provider exposes voices.

tools.description: Complete agent tool allowlist. To attach an Integration Action, use an AgentTool object whose type is connection.

project_count.description: Exact number of projects in the bearer organization.

preset_id.description: Exact catalogue id. `off` has no asset.

asset_version.description: Immutable packaged asset version; it is never inferred.

volume.description: Whole-number selection. Off requires 0; enabled presets require 1 through 100.

AudioEnvironmentInvalidSelection.description: A historic malformed saved pin, returned visibly instead of silently becoming Off. Choose a supported selection or Off before publishing again.

CallerInputEnvironmentSelection.description: Simulation Lab only: a version-pinned condition mixed into the synthetic caller microphone. This is not the agent's outgoing audio_environment and never changes a production call's STT/TTS configuration.

preset_id.description: Exact catalogue id. `off` has no asset and is the quiet baseline.

asset_version.description: Immutable packaged asset version; it is never inferred.

noise_level.description: Whole-number caller-input level. Off requires 0; enabled presets require 1 through 100.

AgentTurnTaking.description: Per-agent barge-in and endpointing tuning. Every field is optional and omitted from responses when it is at its default, so an agent that has never configured this section has no `turn_taking` key at all. Applied when a call starts; saving never changes an in-progress call.

interruption_sensitivity.description: Hosted phone calls in every language. Preset interruption threshold: balanced 500 ms (the default), low 750 ms, high 150 ms. Preset end-of-turn hold on a language with the trained turn detector: balanced 200 ms (the default), low 520 ms, high 260 ms; on a language without one, where the hold is the whole end-of-turn decision: balanced 800 ms (the default), low 1100 ms, high 600 ms. An explicit `min_speech_ms` or `silence_hold_ms` takes precedence over the preset for its knob.

min_speech_ms.description: Hosted phone calls in every language. Explicit continuous-speech threshold before an interruption is considered; it overrides any sensitivity preset. On a phone call the value is honoured down to 150 ms; a value below 150 ms is raised to 150 ms. A phone call with no value set and no sensitivity preset uses the 500 ms default. Browser and web calls do not apply this value at all: it is still stored and returned, but those calls keep the stack's own threshold.

silence_hold_ms.description: Hosted phone calls in every language. Explicit endpointing delay after the caller stops speaking; it overrides the platform default hold and any sensitivity preset.

min_interruption_words.description: Defaults to 1 on hosted ENGLISH phone calls and to 0 everywhere else; set 0 explicitly to disable it. When set, an interruption must ALSO carry at least this many recognized words from the caller, in addition to the speech-duration threshold; it never lowers that threshold. On hosted ENGLISH calls, short listening noises ("mm-hm", "uh-huh", "yeah", "okay", "right", "sure", and filler words such as "uh") do not count toward it, so a caller showing they are following does not interrupt; every word counts in other languages. Not English-only, but effective only on stacks whose transcriber reports words fast enough to land inside the decision window (today the Deepgram stacks, English and Estonian). Elsewhere it is stored, returned unchanged, and ignored at call time.

max_call_seconds.description: How long a call may run before the platform ends it and reports `ended_reason: max_call_duration_reached`. Defaults to 1740 (29 minutes), which is also the ceiling: the underlying media session is dropped at 30 minutes, and a limit above that could never fire, so the call would end with no reason attached. Lower it to cap a call sooner; a value outside the range is refused rather than clamped.

no_caller_speech_seconds.description: How long after the call is answered the platform waits to hear the other party before ending the call and reporting `ended_reason: no_caller_speech_after_answer`. Defaults to 20. Speech is detected from the audio itself, not from a transcript, and once the other party has been heard once the rule does not apply again for the rest of that call. The floor is 10 because the witness is voice activity: a caller who is merely listening looks the same as one who is not there, and a shorter value ends the call partway through the agent's own opening line.

barge_in_speech_rms.description: Deprecated. Accepted, stored and returned for compatibility only; this runtime does not apply it to call behavior. Use `interruption_sensitivity`, `min_speech_ms` and `min_interruption_words` to control interruptions.

AgentOpening.description: Outbound opening policy shared across conversation engines. Only managed outbound telephone calls use this wait; inbound and browser tests retain their normal opening. Saved by voice-stack PATCH and frozen in each call publication. Empty object resets to callee-first with two seconds of observed silence. Speech is allowed to finish beyond this wait. The timer authorizes the opening request, not first audible sound; provider generation and network latency add time.

silence_wait_seconds.description: Silence before requesting the first message when first_speaker is callee. Preserved but unused with agent-first.

AgentVoiceStackUpdate.description: Selection/update payload. It carries only selectors, existing credential IDs, tools, and tuning -- never provider secret material. Supplying languages replaces the selected set; supplying language_profiles replaces sparse overrides, while omission preserves them. After language opt-in, shared prompt, stack, or credential saves explicitly republish inherited effective profiles.

languages.description: When supplied this replaces the selected language set. An engine without a language axis (see voice_frontend and the agent-catalog conversation_engines block) REFUSES this field with 400 rather than accepting and dropping it.

language_profiles.description: When supplied this replaces the sparse override set; omit it to preserve overrides. An engine without a language axis (see voice_frontend and the agent-catalog conversation_engines block) REFUSES this field with 400 rather than accepting and dropping it.

language_profile_revision.description: Optional optimistic-concurrency revision returned by GET. A stale value returns conflict; reload before retrying.

component_credential_bindings.description: Optional stt/llm/tts map to existing hosted-AI credential IDs (or null to use platform-managed selection). References are validated; secret upload is a separate write-only API.

voice_frontend.description: Optional conversation engine. Omitted or cascade is STT/LLM/TTS. gpt_live selects GPT-Live-1. GET still returns transcriber, model, and voice as an OpenAI compatibility projection. Each engine declares whether it has a language axis; a voice-to-voice engine does not, and this route then refuses languages, language_profiles and follow_caller with a 400 naming the field and the engine. Read has_language_axis from the agent-catalog conversation_engines block rather than assuming it from the id.

AgentAnswerDetection.description: What the platform does when a call the carrier reported answered turns out not to be a person: non-human audio such as a caller tune, or a voicemail box. Unlike the other tuning sections, a value you send here is STORED even when it equals the current default, and only an ABSENT `answer_detection` key means "follow the platform default". That is deliberate: the platform default for this setting is expected to change once the detector has been measured, and an agent that explicitly chose a value keeps it when that happens. Applied when a call starts; saving never changes an in-progress call.

non_human_audio.description: `shadow` records what was heard on every answered call and changes nothing the caller experiences: the classification and its detail appear on the call, and no call is ever ended by it. `end_call` acts on the verdict: the agent stops speaking and the call is ended with `ended_reason: no_human_after_answer`, and the classification and its detail appear on the call as they do under `shadow`. `off` collects nothing, so such a call carries no classification at all. `shadow` is the platform default, so it is what an agent with no stored value gets; sending it explicitly stores it, which is how you keep it if that default later moves. This property carries no JSON Schema `default` on purpose, unlike the other tuning properties: a generated client that pre-filled one would send `shadow` on every save and pin a choice the customer never made, which is the one outcome the storage rule above exists to prevent.

voicemail.description: What the AI agent does when a voicemail box answers an outbound call. Voicemail is judged from the first seconds of audio after the answer; the phone network does not report it. Only mailbox-specific evidence counts as proof: a record beep that follows a spoken greeting, or a mailbox instruction such as "leave a message", from a language whose phrase list is verified (en; English is checked on every call). The beep works in every language. The greeting before it must reach three recognised words, counted by the spaces and punctuation between them, so in Chinese, Japanese, Thai and other scripts written without spaces a short greeting is undercounted, and a beep after it only raises suspicion. Candidate phrase lists (de, es, et, fr, ru) are not yet verified: what they recognise is shown as evidence and never proves a mailbox. In any other language only the beep or an English instruction can. A fast answer, a long greeting or music only raise suspicion, and a call the platform is unsure about is treated as a person. `shadow` (watch only) records the verdict and what the platform would have done on the call in Calls, and changes nothing the caller experiences. `hang_up` ends the call without a message on proof of a mailbox. `leave_message` plays the `voicemail_messages` entry for the call's language after the beep, once per contact, and hangs up without a message when there is none for that language. `off` detects nothing. `hang_up` and `leave_message` are accepted and stored now but currently run as `shadow`: they start acting only after the detector has passed its accuracy check, and each call's evidence shows both the chosen and the effective mode. `shadow` is the platform default; like `non_human_audio`, an explicitly sent value is stored even when it equals the default, and this property carries no JSON Schema `default`. The `answer_detection` object is replaced as a whole on save, so send every key you want to keep.

voicemail_messages.description: The messages left when `voicemail` is `leave_message`, one per language, keyed by language code (`{"en": "...", "et": "..."}`); a locale such as `de-DE` is stored as `de`. `leave_message` requires at least one. The message played is the one for the language the call is actually in; a call in a language with no message is ended without one, never given a message in another language. Plain text; runs of whitespace are collapsed, a blank text removes that language's message, and control characters are refused. Each message is played exactly as approved, never improvised by the AI agent, so keep it neutral: who is calling and how to call back, with no account, amount or other personal details, because a voicemail box can be heard by someone other than the person you meant to reach. Messages are kept when `voicemail` changes to another mode and for languages the agent no longer offers.

AgentAcknowledgements.description: Optional short acknowledgement while a slow reply is still being prepared: at most one per caller turn, spoken in the agent's own voice, model and current language on a separate outgoing track, cancelled the moment the real reply starts. Off unless enabled. Without phrases the platform's reviewed list for the call language is used; a language without one stays silent rather than switching to English.

phrases.description: Bounded neutral phrases; digits and currency marks are rejected so a phrase cannot carry a factual, payment, legal or consent claim.

delay_ms.description: How long the reply may take before an acknowledgement is worth speaking.

AgentToolWait.description: What the caller hears while a slow tool call (an integration action, a knowledge search) is still running. Off unless a mode is set. `sound` plays a quiet keyboard-typing bed on the separate outgoing track once the tool has run for `delay_ms`, cut the instant the tool finishes, capped at 15 seconds; it is wordless, so it works in every language. `acknowledge` speaks one short phrase in the agent's own voice and language instead; without phrases the platform's reviewed list for the call language is used, and a language without one stays silent. Feedback never plays over the caller or the agent, at most once per tool wait, and never for the built-in end-call or transfer tools.

delay_ms.description: How long a tool may run before feedback starts. Most tools finish well inside this.

phrases.description: For `acknowledge` only; the same bounded neutral-phrase rule as acknowledgements. Rejected with `sound`.

AgentUnrecognisedSpeech.description: What the agent does when the caller speaks and the transcriber produces nothing at all — most often a caller using a language the agent's transcriber is not listening for, but also a bad line or a dropout. The agent says one short line in the call's own language telling the caller it could not understand them and which languages it can help in, then keeps listening; it never guesses what was said, never calls a tool and never ends the call. It is spoken only after the caller has stopped talking and the platform's wait for a transcript has expired, so it cannot talk over a live caller, and it is skipped entirely on an agent with follow-the-caller enabled, where the language switch answers instead. On by default, and spoken at most twice per call unless you change `max_per_call`. Send `enabled: false` to switch it off; an absent section is the default and is not stored.

enabled.description: `false` switches the line off for this agent, and is the only value stored: the behaviour is on for every agent that says nothing.

phrase.description: Your own wording, spoken verbatim in place of the line the agent would otherwise compose in the call's language. Write it in the agent's language: it is not translated.

max_per_call.description: How many times one call may hear it. Two when unset.

AgentModelUnresponsive.description: How long the agent may stay silent after the caller has finished speaking before the platform ends the call. It exists because a conversation engine can stop answering without saying so: a provider outage mid-call leaves the line up, the caller talking to nobody and the call billing, and on some engines nothing at all is reported. It counts only time the line was free: the clock starts when a caller turn ends, it does NOT run while the caller is speaking (their own speech is subtracted, so a caller who keeps talking is never cut off mid-sentence, and one who pauses between attempts still reaches the bound), and it is cleared the moment the agent produces anything — a reply, a tool call, or the end of the call. It also never runs while the agent is speaking, while a tool is running, before the caller's first turn, or on a call whose replies come from a workflow. A call ended this way reports `ended_reason` `agent_unresponsive` with `reason_detail` `model_unresponsive` (calls completed before 2026-09-25 reported `model_session_lost` with the same detail). On by default at the platform's own bound; an absent section is that default and is not stored.

seconds.description: The bound, in seconds. `0` switches it off, and is the only value outside the range: an agent that waits on something genuinely slow may need it. Otherwise 10 to 120. The platform's own bound applies when unset.

AgentVoicePolish.description: Per-agent voice polish. Absent keys keep the platform defaults; the response omits the section entirely when nothing is configured.

delivery.description: How the selected voice performs its speech. Unset keeps the provider's own defaults, which is what every agent had before this field existed. Each profile maps to allowlisted provider controls only where the selected TTS provider/model truthfully exposes them: ElevenLabs voice settings (eleven_v3 supports stability only), a bounded Gemini TTS synthesis instruction, and a speaking-rate multiplier for Soniox and Cartesia. Fish Audio and Azure neural voices accept the setting but apply no change. The voice preview (POST /v1/voice-previews with the same `delivery`) uses the identical mapping, so an audition sounds like the call.

AgentVoiceStack.description: Safe read projection. It never includes component credential binding IDs, plaintext/ciphertext, nonce, fingerprint, or provider secrets.

voice.description: The stored TTS selection as the agent catalog projects it, including `delivery_control` (`voice_settings`, `instruction`, `speed` or `unsupported`): whether a `voice_polish.delivery` profile changes this voice's audio, and `delivery_profiles`: the exact value each profile resolves to on this engine (empty for `unsupported`), both read from the packaged delivery table.

voice_frontend.description: The conversation engine; cascade is the default. Always present on GET; omitted on older rows means cascade. Whether this engine has a language axis is declared in the agent-catalog conversation_engines block (has_language_axis).

Clients cannot supply runtime adapter options, bindings, or rates.

A selected multilingual hosted language chooses one allowed published profile before reservation. For a multilingual hosted agent, language selects an allowed published profile before reserve and worker dispatch. CallRecordingState.description: Safe recording-disclosure state (services/calls_routing/calls.py:_call_recording_state_from_rows). recording_state and recording_disclosure on Call both carry this same object.

status.description: not_started or disabled when there is no recording yet, otherwise the latest recording's own status (e.g. processing, available, deleted).

recording_id.description: Empty string when there is no recording yet.

active_recording_id.description: Empty string unless the latest recording is undeleted and available.

media_url.description: Empty string unless a recording is currently active.

CallRecording.description: Metadata for the active recording. Use download_url for playback; storage_key and media_url are legacy implementation details, not download contracts.

download_url.description: Relative authenticated API URL for full or byte-range recording playback.

CallWorkflow.description: Where a call's conversation workflow ended, read the same way on the call detail, MCP get_call and the call.completed / call.failed webhooks. Ids, platform and author-declared strings, and the author's outcome label only; never a call value. The vocabularies are open: a later release may add values, so handle unknown ones. On a webhook this is a snapshot at emission; GET /v1/calls/{call_id} is the current read, and `settled` says whether it can still change. To act on a request not to be contacted, check `"cease_contact" in interrupts`: it is the one canonical stop signal, and nothing adds the number to the do-not-call register by itself.

version.description: The published version the run pinned; null when it pinned the draft (a Talk test or an inbound Phone test). A step_id resolves after later edits only against a published version.

status.description: Known values: running (the call is in progress), completed, transferred, failed (the workflow itself failed), incomplete (it stopped before completing or transferring, typically because the call ended first).

settled.description: true once the run is closed and nothing can change this object; false while a turn could still commit. An incomplete run on an ended call can be unsettled, can still change, and can stay unsettled: treat it as not final.

step_id.description: The last outcome step the run reached, as authored.

type.description: The step's declared outcome type. Known values: review_candidate, informational, terminal_note.

label.description: The step's label: display text the author can change. Never match on it.

outcome.description: The step reached; null when the run reached no outcome step.

interrupts.description: Every distinct global interrupt the run took, in the order first taken; [] when none. Known values: wrong_party, dispute, hardship, cease_contact, callback, human_request, language_change. An interrupt is what the caller said that the workflow acted on; it can differ from the outcome reached (an interrupt may lead to an ask or a transfer, and a run can take one and later end on an ordinary route).

CallDetail.description: The call GET /v1/calls/{call_id} returns: the Call resource plus where its workflow ended. The GET /v1/calls list returns Call without it.

workflow.description: null when the call ran no workflow (every GPT-Live and Gemini Live call).

Call.description: The call resource GET /v1/calls returns, and GET /v1/calls/{call_id} returns as CallDetail (this plus workflow). A synthetic simulation or platform-internal room is never returned here; only a call the customer or their agent actually made.

direction.description: inbound, outbound, or web_test (a live browser test) for a call your agent placed or answered. A call seeded by the demo/artifact-import tooling can carry other values, such as imported, verbatim from that import.

status.description: Call lifecycle status, e.g. requested, queued, dialing, ringing, answered, in_progress, media_started, completed, failed, busy, no_answer, canceled, live_blocked, policy_blocked, needs_review (held for review: never dialled, with a call.failed at once). Not a closed set: track it as an opaque string and rely on the call.* events for exact transitions.

browser_outcome.description: Specific-call detail only. A managed workspace browser worker's frozen outcome, readable before transport completion. Empty means unknown. browser_startup_failed means the requested opening failed before observed agent output; worker_ended confirms worker teardown. Neither changes transport status or promises a refund.

ended_reason.description: Why the call ended. `browser_startup_failed` means a workspace browser test requested an opening that failed before observed agent output; it does not promise a refund. `funding_exhausted` means the last funded runtime allowance expired; `reason_detail` is `insufficient_balance` for a confirmed funding refusal or `renewal_unavailable` when renewal could not be confirmed. Holds estimate usage and do not cap the final cost. Other reasons fall into three groups. Two are the ordinary end of a call that went well: `agent_completed` when the agent finished the conversation and ended the call itself, which is the usual outcome of a workflow that runs to its last step, and `remote_party_disconnected` when the other party hung up. Six are endings the platform initiates: `agent_unresponsive`, described below, `hangup_requested` when someone ends the call from the workspace or through POST /v1/calls/{call_id}/hangup, `max_call_duration_reached` when the call hits its configured limit, `no_caller_speech_after_answer` when the call is answered but nobody ever speaks, `no_human_after_answer` when the call is answered but nothing on the line was a person: only music or tones were ever heard, or a recording repeated the same cycle of things over and over, and `caller_unresponsive` when both sides fell silent after the agent had spoken: after 30 seconds of silence the agent asks whether the caller is still there (once per silent stretch, at most three times per call), and the call ends politely 15 seconds after that question if nobody answers. This ending is rolling out: while it is in observation the platform records what it would have done and does not end calls, so the value does not yet appear. A caller who answers, even with one word, simply continues the conversation. The last two name an ending nobody chose, neither the people on the call nor the platform: `media_session_lost`, when the media session went away underneath a live call -- the room was deleted, or the connection to it failed -- and `model_session_lost`, when the conversation engine behind the call failed and could not be recovered while the media session was still up, so the platform ended the call rather than leave the line open with nobody on it. `agent_unresponsive` is the platform ending a call whose agent stopped answering while its engine stayed connected: the caller finished speaking and the agent produced nothing for the whole of the agent's `voice_polish.model_unresponsive` bound, which counts only the time the caller was NOT speaking. It reports `reason_detail` `model_unresponsive`. It says what was observed -- a silent agent -- and not that anything failed, because a voice-to-voice engine reports nothing when it stops answering. Calls completed before 2026-09-25 reported this ending as `model_session_lost` with the same `reason_detail`. In all three, nobody hung up, no limit fired and the agent did not finish. Each reports what was observed rather than guessing at a cause, so a call that ends this way is not reported as an operator hang-up even when an operator had just asked for one; that request is answered separately and says the call was already gone. Empty on a call that completed before this field shipped, and on a call that has not completed. A call that FAILED reports its reason in `technical_failure.failure_reason_code` instead; the two vocabularies are separate.

answer_classification.description: What was heard after the call was answered, which is a different question from whether it was answered at all: a carrier bridges audio for a ringback replacement tune or a hold-music loop exactly as it does for a person, so the status says the line answered and this says what was on it. `human` means a person was heard. `non_human_audio` means nothing a person did was ever heard: continuous music or tones held the line, or a recording repeated the same cycle of things over and over; `reason_detail` names which kind. `silent` means the line answered and nothing at all was heard. `unknown` means the detector ran and reached no decision inside its window, which is deliberately NOT the same as the empty string: empty means no verdict was reported at all, on a call placed before this field shipped, on an agent whose collection is switched off, or on a call whose media never started. Detection is deliberately narrow and only claims `non_human_audio` for unbroken non-human audio, so a recorded announcement or an IVR menu with pauses in it reads as `human` or `unknown` rather than being classified here -- unless it repeats itself, which is the one text-based verdict, `looping_recording`.

reason_detail.description: Qualifies either `answer_classification` or `ended_reason`, and says which by the value. `insufficient_balance` and `renewal_unavailable` qualify only `funding_exhausted`: confirmed insufficient funds versus unavailable authorization, respectively. `caller_tune`, `hold_music` and `looping_recording` appear only with `answer_classification` `non_human_audio`, and `no_audio` only with `silent`: `looping_recording` means the far end said the same cycle of things over and over, a recording on repeat, rather than music or tones. `model_unresponsive` appears with `ended_reason` `agent_unresponsive` -- and, on calls completed before 2026-09-25, with `model_session_lost` -- and means the call was ended by the platform because the agent produced nothing at all for the whole of its bound of caller-free time after the caller finished speaking -- as opposed to the same reason reached because the conversation engine reported its own failure. Empty when neither needs qualifying, which is most calls. This is not `ended_reason` itself: that one names the ending, this one adds to it.

agents_returned.description: Present only when agent_window was requested: agents in this page.

agents_has_more.description: Present only when agent_window was requested. True when the organization has more agents than this page holds; the page is NOT the whole set unless this is false.

agents_next_cursor.description: Present only when agent_window was requested. Non-empty only when agents_has_more is true: pass it as agent_after to continue. Empty string on the last page.

SmsMessage.description: recipient_type is optional and never enforced; there is no recipient_type column on the SMS row, so it is accepted but not persisted. Blocked categories mirror carrier acceptable-use policy; debt collection is not a blocked category -- payment_reminder (first-party or third-party) is permitted with per-call authorization, subject to per-customer onboarding approval and the acceptable-use policy.

recipient_type.description: Optional, never enforced or required -- outbound is not restricted to business recipients. Persisted verbatim on the call row if sent; SMS has no recipient_type column, so it is accepted but not stored there.

purpose.description: Required, free-form outbound purpose declaration -- a non-empty purpose is the compliance paper trail; a novel purpose token is never refused for being novel. Documented catalog (pick one or send your own token): appointment, booking_confirmation, callback_requested, customer_outreach, delivery_notification, ops_alert, other, payment_reminder, personal_errand, reservation, status_check, support.

organization_id.description: Optional. Defaults to the authenticated principal's own organization. When supplied it must match it; another workspace is refused.

project_id.description: Optional. Defaults to the organization's first project. When supplied it must belong to that organization.

from_phone_number.description: Caller ID in E.164, resolved inside the deployment's own project.

from_number_id.description: Caller ID by number id; must be an active number of the deployment's project.

agent_id.description: Defaults to the caller number's own configured agent.

VariablesConfig.title: VariablesConfig
VariablesConfig.description: An agent's call variables, SMS templates and caller lookup. Exported from config_schema.py (the API's copy; tests pin the two equal) for the dashboard and the docs. tests/fixtures/call_variables/config_cases.json is the accept/reject contract.

text.description: Text per language. The agent's primary language is required; any other language falls back to it.

revision.description: The agent's latest published language-profile version; send it back as base_revision. Any publish of the agent moves it. 0 before the agent is first published.

schema_hash.description: sha256 of the variable schema a call admitted now would carry; empty when the publication declares none a call could be admitted with.

published_at.description: When the current publication was made; empty before the first.

base_revision.description: The revision this edit was based on. When sent and stale, the write is refused with 409 revision_conflict. Omit for last-write-wins.

AgentTemplateMessage.description: Everything POST /v1/messages takes that names no resource, plus the template and what fills it. body, campaign_id, provider and segment_count are refused. The sending number, under any of its names, must belong to the agent's project.

project_id.description: Optional. The agent's own project; any other answers 404 exactly as a foreign agent does.

language.description: The language to send in. Text is chosen from the call or request language, then its base language (et-EE -> et), then the agent's primary language, then, as a last resort, the template's texts in language-code order.

variables.description: Values for the agent's declared variables the template references. A referenced required variable must be present; protected variables are refused (there is no confirmation to lean on).

slots.description: Values for the template's model slots, each within its max_length.

purpose.description: The message's purpose, authorized as on POST /v1/messages.

to.description: The recipient, E.164. to_phone_number is accepted as its alias.

has_more.description: True while older rows remain. A page is the whole list only when this is false.

next_cursor.description: Send as `cursor` to read the next page; null on the last page.

last_message.description: The conversation's newest message, as GET /v1/messages returns it; absent when it has none.

TranslationRequest.description: Idempotent for the current source revision and target. Repeating the command reuses the saved result; no client-generated idempotency key is needed.

source_completeness.description: Partial indicates interrupted artifact delivery or unsettled source data; any available original text remains readable.

quote_pending.description: The settled source is waiting for its current-revision word-count summary. Poll this pure read; quote is absent until ready.

quote.description: Pre-inference upper bound using all original words. Language detection can reduce the settled price. Absent for unavailable or unquoted summary sources.

pagination.description: Selected call translation units follow the original transcript timeline's pages.

id.description: The immutable original turn or message id.

text.description: Original text; null with unavailable_reason for an oversized unit.

translated_text.description: Cached text for this exact original ID and revision; null when unavailable.

CallTranscriptStreamPage.description: JSON envelope containing an ordered event page, with the NDJSON content type label preserved.

working_hours.description: Monday=0 through Sunday=6; each value is [start,end] in local minutes since midnight. No overnight intervals.
